clause_i.reason: For D equal to every simplified-mode shutter_hold attempt after camera, zoom, and focus preparation, the challenge-derived event offset is not available to an observation-free policy. Identical prior actions and task times can arrive at an active or inactive event phase across generated instances, so no q(I_t) can always select the delayed shutter start or safe no-op action.

clause_ii.reason: With the configured 800 ms, six-frame window, g can use the visible target trajectory and the expanding-ring phase to predict whether delivery 400 ms later leaves at least the 1020 ms hold inside the active event; it starts the shutter when that remains optimal and otherwise preserves the next loop with no-op. The simplified pan/zoom/focus surface does not change this bounded-window shutter witness.

clause_iii.reason: Choose an active-event history with 1120 ms remaining, which is 100 ms more than the 1020 ms minimum hold. Starting the shutter now can qualify, but after tau=200 ms the same shutter_start has only 920 ms of active event left and cannot qualify, while the next 7200 ms loop remains available. The changing target/ring state is visible in the recent frames and causes the strict loss.
